adjudication_records.issue_text: Post#cook returns raw verbatim for cook_method == :raw_html (app/models/post.rb:131) and app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 renders raw post.cooked, so third-party feed/Readability HTML is stored and served with no sanitization

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff explicitly introduces a bypass of the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` using HTML taken from RSS (`SimpleRSS.parse ... i.content`) or Readability (`doc.content`) (app/models/topic_embed.rb, app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). In the embed UI, `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders that content with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so the imported third-party HTML is served without escaping/sanitization, enabling stored XSS in the embedded iframe/page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CGI.unescapeHTML on feed item content in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 converts escaped markup back into live HTML that is stored as raw_html, producing stored XSS

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passes that into `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` short-circuits to `return raw` for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and for `raw_html` posts `cooked == raw`, so any HTML produced by `CGI.unescapeHTML` (e.g. `<script>...`) becomes live markup and is stored/served back, enabling stored XSS via a malicious feed item.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 assumes embed.post is present, but it is nil for a trashed post (Trashable default scope), so PostRevisor.new(post) blows up; no dependent: cleanup or FK on topic_embeds permanently breaks re-import of that URL

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then unconditionally does `post = embed.post` and, if the content hash differs, calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!`. There is no guard for `post` being `nil`. Since the migration adds no foreign key and the model has no dependent cleanup, it’s possible for a `topic_embeds` row to exist whose `post_id` no longer points to a visible/valid `Post` record (e.g., hard-deleted post, or an association hidden by a default scope/soft-delete). In that case `embed.post` would be `nil` and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` would raise, preventing re-import/updates for that URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28 uses setnx followed by a separate expire, which is not atomic; a worker crash between calls leaves the key forever and throttles that embed URL permanently

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, throttling is implemented via `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two calls are not atomic. If the worker/process crashes or is killed after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will be left without a TTL. On subsequent calls, `setnx` will return false (key already exists) and the method will return `true`, causing `retrieve` to be permanently throttled for that specific `@embed_url` (until manual Redis cleanup).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:37 and app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 use exists?/where(...).first followed by create!, a TOCTOU against the unique index on embed_url that raises unhandled ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique under concurrency

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. The diff introduces a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). But both `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` and `TopicEmbed.import` perform a read-then-create sequence without handling races:

- `lib/topic_retriever.rb` `perform_retrieve` does `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and then later may call `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which can lead to creation.
- `app/models/topic_embed.rb` `import` does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank, within a transaction creates a post and then calls `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`.

Under concurrency, two workers/processes can both observe no existing row and then both attempt `create!`; the second will hit the unique index and raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. There is no rescue/retry/upsert logic, so this is an unhandled correctness defect (TOCTOU) introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 uses create_table ... force: true, which silently drops a pre-existing table; the same change was retro-fitted into the already-shipped 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` in the new migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`, and also changes an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails migrations, `force: true` drops an existing table before creating it, which can cause silent data loss if the migration is run in an environment where the table already exists (e.g., partial/failed migrations, manual table creation, re-running migrations). The finding accurately points out this risky behavior and the retrofit into an already-shipped migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 declares embed_url as t.string (varchar(255)), so URLs longer than 255 chars raise 'value too long' and kill the import job

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds.embed_url` as `t.string` with no explicit `limit`, which in Rails maps to a VARCHAR(255) on common DBs. In the diff, `TopicEmbed.import` and `EmbedController#best` accept arbitrary `embed_url` values from params/RSS (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url)`, `TopicEmbed.create!`). If an embed URL exceeds 255 characters, inserting/updating `embed_url` will raise a DB error (e.g., value too long) and, since jobs/controllers don’t rescue it here, it would fail the import/request. This is a real schema-vs-input correctness risk introduced by the diff, even if it only manifests for long URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 adds a column with a non-null default to posts, rewriting the whole table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on Postgres < 11

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds migration `AddCookMethodToPosts` with `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT <non-null> ...` typically rewrites the entire table and takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration, which can block reads/writes on a large `posts` table and cause downtime. This behavior is directly implied by the migration shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inline on every embed cache miss, re-fetching and re-importing the entire feed just to find one URL

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb, `perform_retrieve` synchronously runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true and the specific `@embed_url` is not already in `topic_embeds`.

`Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) fetches the full feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and iterates all `rss.items`, calling `TopicEmbed.import(...)` for each item. This means a single embed URL cache miss can trigger a full feed fetch and (attempted) import of every feed entry, which is redundant if the goal is only to resolve one URL. The behavior is directly present in the diff and is a clear performance/efficiency defect (even though it is conditional on feed polling being enabled and it runs inside the retrieve job, not the controller action).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 hard-requires a Referer header, so legitimate embeds are rejected with a 403 InvalidAccess when browsers omit it (HTTPS→HTTP, Referrer-Policy), and the host comparison is case-sensitive so mixed-case hosts fail

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is gated by `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. If the `Referer` header is missing (e.g., due to HTTPS→HTTP referrer suppression or Referrer-Policy), `request.referer` becomes `nil`, `URI('')` yields `host == nil`, and the code always raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` (rejecting otherwise legitimate embeds). Also, the host comparison is a plain string equality check with no normalization; hostnames are case-insensitive, so a mixed-case referer host vs a lowercase `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` would be rejected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.css.scss and embed.js are new top-level manifests not referenced by application.css/application.js and not added to config.assets.precompile, so stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' raises AssetFilteredError and the embed page 500s in production

spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18 and :24 stub only their own setting while feed_polling_enabled? defaults to false, so the && short-circuits and both tests pass vacuously; poll_feed itself is stubbed out in every test and never exercised

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute the guard is `poll_feed if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? && SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? && SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?`. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the tests "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" only stub one setting each (feed_polling_url / embed_by_username) and do not stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true. Given the defaults added in config/site_settings.yml set `feed_polling_enabled: false`, the condition short-circuits on `feed_polling_enabled?` and the expectations `poll_feed.never` pass regardless of the stubbed setting, so those tests don’t actually verify the intended requirement. Also, every example mocks `poll_feed` via `expects`, so `poll_feed` is never executed in this spec file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8 'is 404 without an embed_url' passes because the default empty embeddable_host makes ensure_embeddable raise before params.require runs, leaving missing-param behavior untested

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController`, `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` runs before the `best` action body. `ensure_embeddable` raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` if `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?`. The diff sets the default `embeddable_host` to `''` in `config/site_settings.yml`, so in the spec `get :best` (without params and without stubbing `embeddable_host`) will fail due to the before_filter, never reaching `params.require(:embed_url)`. Therefore `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`'s "is 404 without an embed_url" can pass without actually testing the missing-parameter behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:24 checks post.present?, which is always true for an ActiveRecord instance even when unsaved with errors, so a failed PostCreator leads to TopicEmbed.create! raising a NOT NULL violation instead of a meaningful error

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import the code does `post = creator.create` and then guards `TopicEmbed.create!` with `if post.present?`. The finding assumes `creator.create` returns an unsaved ActiveRecord instance on failure, making `post.present?` “always true” and causing NOT NULL violations from `post.id/topic_id` being nil. That behavior is not verifiable from this diff: PostCreator#create’s return contract isn’t shown, and existing code in the repo (e.g., the prior disqus importer) also used `post = creator.create` followed by `if post.present?`, implying create returns nil/false (or raises) on failure. Also, `present?` is not “always true” here because `post` can be nil. Therefore the claimed defect depends on speculative behavior outside the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 uses href.start_with?('/'), which also matches protocol-relative URLs so //cdn.example.com/x.png is rewritten and broken, while relative URLs without a leading slash are left untouched

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the code rewrites any href/src that `start_with?('/')` by prefixing the embed page’s scheme/host and stripping all leading slashes (`href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`). This condition is also true for protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png`, which would be rewritten to something like `http://<embed-host>/cdn.example.com/x.png`, breaking the intended external CDN URL. Additionally, the method claims to convert relative URLs but only handles root-relative paths (starting with `/`), leaving other valid relatives (e.g., `images/x.png`) untouched.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:59 checks uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443, dropping the port for http://host:443 and https://host:80 and producing a wrong prefix; compare against the scheme's default port

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the prefix is built as "#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}" and then the port is appended only if `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`. This condition omits the port whenever it is 80 or 443, regardless of scheme. For non-default combinations like `http://example.com:443/...` or `https://example.com:80/...`, the port would be incorrectly dropped, producing wrong absolute URLs in rewritten href/src values. The finding is directly verifiable from the diff and is a real correctness bug for such URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: open(...) in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 and app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 has no read_timeout/open_timeout and no size cap, so a slow or huge remote endpoint hangs the Sidekiq worker indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces remote fetching via `open-uri` in two new code paths: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (called by `TopicRetriever` and disqus import). Neither call supplies `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` options nor enforces any maximum response size, and `import_remote` reads the entire body into memory. This creates a verifiable reliability/DoS risk where a slow/streaming or very large response can tie up a Sidekiq worker for a long time and/or exhaust memory. (The “indefinitely” wording may be overstated because Net::HTTP has defaults, but the absence of explicit limits/timeouts is real in the diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117,143 drops the documented --category/-c option and the created_at: Date.parse(...) value when switching to TopicEmbed.import_remote, losing original topic dates; import_remote has no rescue so one 404 aborts the entire import

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and no longer computes/uses `category_id`, so the previously supported `--category/-c` option is indeed dropped. It also replaces `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` only uses `opts[:title]` (and fetches remote HTML) with no handling for `created_at` or category, so imported topics will no longer preserve the original thread date or chosen category. Additionally, `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` without any rescue; since the thor task also doesn’t rescue around `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, a single network/HTTP error (e.g., 404) would raise and can terminate the import run. All of these are directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12 has no null check on document.getElementById('discourse-comments'), so comments.appendChild throws and breaks the host page's JS when the container is missing or the script runs in <head>

adjudication.rationale: In new app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, it unconditionally does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then immediately calls `comments.appendChild(iframe);` with no guard. If the element is missing (wrong ID, script included on a page without the container) or the script runs before the DOM element exists (e.g., loaded in <head> without defer/DOMContentLoaded), `comments` will be null and `appendChild` will throw a TypeError, potentially breaking the host page’s JS execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 defines feed_key (the SHA1 feed-modified cache key) as dead code; no conditional GET is performed, so every hourly poll re-downloads and re-hashes the full feed

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb a method `feed_key` is defined (building a SHA1-based Redis key for the feed URL) but it is never called anywhere in the diff. The actual `poll_feed` implementation always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no use of `feed_key`, no Redis lookup, and no conditional request logic (e.g., If-Modified-Since/ETag), so each scheduled run will re-fetch the full feed regardless of whether it changed. The only SHA1 hashing performed in the job is for the key inside the unused `feed_key` method, so the “re-hashes the full feed” phrasing is slightly off, but the core point (dead code + no conditional/cached polling) is verifiably true from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1 has an unrelated require_dependency 'email/sender' (copy-paste) that needlessly eager-loads the mail stack in the worker

adjudication.rationale: In the new file `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, the top lines include `require_dependency 'email/sender'`, but the job’s `execute` method never references `Email::Sender` (it only looks up a `User` and calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`). This makes the require unrelated to the job’s logic and therefore an unnecessary load introduced by the diff (likely copy/paste).
